rows.selection_reason: With no prior evidence, the first experiment should establish a strong multimodal baseline using the highest-capacity choices across all design dimensions: scgpt (pretrained single-cell foundation model) for RNA, imagenet_vit_l (largest image encoder) for images, transformer aggregation (most expressive for multiprofile), and weighted fusion (most flexible modality combining). This tests whether the full multimodal pipeline can achieve strong validation accuracy and provides a ceiling reference. If it performs well, subsequent experiments can ablate individual components (encoder, aggregation, fusion) to identify what drives performance. If it underperforms, it signals that complexity is a bottleneck and simpler alternatives (e.g., resnet50, avgpool, concat) should be explored. This is the most informative single experiment under a 10-run budget because it simultaneously validates the multimodal hypothesis and anchors the search space.

Evidence: Our only completed experiment (config_015) achieved ~52% accuracy with multimodal/multiprofile/scgpt/imagenet_vit_l/transformer/weighted. This is a single data point, so we have high uncertainty about which components are driving performance. Question: config_012 is a single-variable change from config_015, swapping imagenet_vit_l for resnet50 while keeping all other settings identical (scgpt, transformer, weighted, multiprofile). This directly tests whether the stronger image encoder (ViT-L) is a critical contributor or whether a simpler CNN (ResNet50) suffices. Why this is the best next experiment: The image encoder is a high-impact architectural choice that appears in many of the remaining untested configurations. Resolving whether imagenet_vit_l is necessary will (a) confirm or eliminate a key design constraint for the remaining 8 experiments, and (b) if resnet50 performs comparably, free us to explore other dimensions (aggregation, fusion, RNA encoder) without the heavier ViT-L. This clean A/B test maximizes information gain per experiment under our tight budget.

Evidence: config_015 (scgpt, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted) achieved 0.520 accuracy, and config_012 (same but resnet50) achieved 0.494, confirming that imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted + multiprofile is the strongest architecture so far. Uncertainty: we have only tested scgpt as the RNA encoder; scvi_n200 (a variational autoencoder) encodes RNA very differently and may capture complementary or superior biological signal. This experiment (config_026: scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted, multimodal, multiprofile) is a clean single-variable swap against our current best, isolating the RNA encoder effect. It is the best use of experiment 3 because the RNA encoder is the highest-leverage untested design choice within the already-validated architecture, and resolving it early (with 7 experiments left) lets us commit the remaining budget to refining the winning combination rather than exploring a suboptimal RNA encoder.

Evidence: config_026 (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted) achieved 0.725 accuracy, far surpassing scgpt-based configs (~0.50-0.52), establishing scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer as the strongest combination. Uncertainty: whether weighted fusion or concat fusion better leverages the strong scvi_n200 representations when combined with transformer aggregation. This experiment (config_016) tests concat fusion while holding all other hyperparameters at their best-known values, isolating the fusion mechanism as the single variable. It is the best next step because it is a minimal, clean ablation on the top-performing config—exploiting the strong evidence for scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer while resolving a key architectural uncertainty that could push accuracy above 0.725 in the remaining 6 experiments.

The strongest evidence so far is that scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted (config_026, acc=0.7250) is the best configuration, with concat fusion (config_016, acc=0.7207) nearly matching it. The only aggregation tested with this top encoder pair is 'transformer'. Config_047 (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, weighted) isolates the aggregation method while holding the best-known encoders and fusion fixed. This tells us whether the transformer aggregation is a critical contributor or whether a simpler avgpool suffices—reducing uncertainty about a key architectural dimension. If avgpool performs comparably, we free up design flexibility; if it degrades significantly, we confirm transformer aggregation is essential and can focus remaining budget on other axes (e.g., profile setting or alternative RNA encoders). With 5 experiments left, this minimal-change test is the highest-information next step before committing to further exploitation.

Evidence: scvi_n200 is clearly the dominant RNA encoder (0.725 vs 0.520 for scgpt), and the current best (config_026: scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted, acc=0.725) uses a large ViT image encoder. However, the image encoder gap was modest with scgpt (0.520 vs 0.494, only ~2.6 pts), so its contribution in the scvi_n200 regime is uncertain. This experiment (scvi_n200 + resnet50 + transformer + weighted) tests whether the smaller resnet50 image encoder is competitive when paired with the strong scvi_n200 RNA encoder. If resnet50 performs comparably, it confirms the RNA encoder is the primary driver and we can focus remaining budget on other axes (e.g., singleprofile vs multiprofile, PCA). If it drops significantly, it confirms imagenet_vit_l is essential and we should lock in the current best architecture. This is the best use of experiment 6 because it directly reduces uncertainty about the second most important design variable in the context of the proven best RNA encoder, and it is a logical exploitation of the current leading direction before spending remaining budget on more speculative changes.

Evidence: scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted (config_026, acc=0.725) is the clear best, and all completed experiments use multiprofile. The singleprofile setting is completely unexplored, creating significant uncertainty about whether the multiprofile+transformer architecture is actually necessary or if a simpler single-profile model with the same encoders could match or exceed it. This experiment (config_017: scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + singleprofile + weighted) directly tests that hypothesis using the best-validated RNA and image encoders. It is the best use of this slot because: (1) it reduces uncertainty on a major untested architectural dimension, (2) if it performs comparably, it confirms a simpler viable path for remaining experiments, and (3) if it underperforms significantly, it confirms the multiprofile+transformer design is essential, allowing the final 3 experiments to focus purely on exploiting the multiprofile space (e.g., testing pca_n2000 as RNA encoder or fine-tuning fusion). No other untested configuration offers as much information per experiment under the remaining budget.

The current best (config_026: scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted + multiprofile, acc=0.7250) has been identified, and all remaining scvi_n200 multimodal-multiprofile variants involve known-negative changes (avgpool, concat, resnet50, singleprofile) unlikely to exceed it. The key remaining uncertainty is whether pca_n2000, the only untested RNA encoder in the optimal multimodal-multiprofile setting, could be competitive. config_029 (pca_n2000 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted + multiprofile) is a clean single-factor swap from config_026, directly testing whether the learned scvi representation is truly necessary or whether a linear PCA projection suffices. Given only 2 experiments remain, this is the highest-information experiment: if pca_n2000 is competitive (~0.70+), it reveals an alternative design axis for the final experiments; if it is substantially worse (as scgpt was at 0.52), it confirms scvi_n200 is essential and the current best is near-optimal, allowing the last two experiments to focus on fine-grained fusion/aggregation tweaks around the known optimum.

Evidence: config_026 (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted) is the clear best at 0.7250, with config_016 (same but concat) at 0.7207 and config_010 (resnet50, transformer, weighted) at 0.7131. The top-performing region is firmly scvi_n200 + multiprofile + transformer. Question: config_032 (scvi_n200, resnet50, transformer, concat) is the last untested cell in the 2×2 image_encoder×fusion grid under transformer aggregation with scvi_n200. Testing it completes the picture of whether any transformer-aggregation variant could edge out config_026, or confirms it as the ceiling. Why this is best: With only 1 experiment remaining after this one, I need to either (a) discover a configuration that beats 0.7250 to guide the final experiment, or (b) confirm config_026 is optimal so the last experiment can be spent on a different exploratory axis. config_032 is the highest-information test within the proven high-performing region—any unexpected result would redirect the final experiment, while a confirmed lower result locks in config_026 as the answer and frees the last slot for broader exploration.

Evidence strongly favors scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + multiprofile as the top-performing family (config_026: 0.7250, config_016: 0.7207, config_047: 0.7062). The 2x2 design over aggregation (transformer/avgpool) × fusion (weighted/concat) for this encoder pair is now fully tested except for avgpool+concat. Since this is the final experiment (10 of 10), the goal is to either beat the current best (0.7250) or confirm the design-space optimum. Config_045 (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, concat) is the only remaining untested combination of the two best encoders with multiprofile. While transformer+weighted is favored, testing the last cell in this 2x2 grid completes the evidence and has the highest ceiling among all remaining options, as all other untested configs involve weaker encoders (resnet50, scgpt, pca_n2000) or singleprofile, which have shown substantially lower performance.
